notes: Accept. 111 items, 99 missing and 12 planned, every missing item routed exactly once and four planned items named as sources. I reproduced the recorded hash of arXiv v3 (167574c8…), the accepted version. All stages named by the four source routes exist, and so do all eleven planned layer ids. All 88 locator checks land where they say once statements and their proofs are distinguished: the four apparent exceptions are locators that name a proof (Lemma 3.2 stated on p. 24 with its proof on p. 25; Proposition 4.8 on p. 37 with its proof on p. 38; Lemma 9.4 on p. 65 with its proof on p. 66). The twelve findings are misprints, and the sample I checked is verbatim: Lemma 1.8 does say 'the centralizer of δ in U(W)' while its own conclusion is about U(V); §3's introduction literally prints 'That this implies Theorem 2.12 is Proposition Prop: initial reduction', an unresolved LaTeX label leaking into the text; Remark 4.4 does write 'Gordan' for Julia Gordon; §7.3 does write 'g ∈ GL_n(F)' inside a description of U(V_y) ⊂ GL_{n+1}(F) × GL_{n+1}(F); and §11.1 does attribute to H′(F_v) × H′(F_v) the invariant polynomials of the H(F_v)-action, in a sentence whose second half gets the primed case right. One observation for the maintainer rather than a defect of this extraction: both Part II routes give area 'modular', which is not a galaxy id in data/galaxies.json — it is an atlas group. This is a corpus-wide pattern, not this paper's: fifteen routes across the extractions use 'modular', including the four other proposals of this same roadmap, and 'cohomology', 'algebra', 'motivic', 'classical', 'diophantine' and 'numbertheory' are used elsewhere with the same problem. check_paper.py only requires the area to be non-empty, so nothing catches it. Re-tagging this paper alone would desynchronise it from the four extractions it deliberately agrees with, so I left it and record the pattern here. Nothing was corrected, rejected or deleted.
